# Goal

Recover global plot coordinates in metres from a scanned paper map: click labelled points and controls, then use homography (preferred) or affine transformation (Plan B). These transformations assume a planar map; they do not repair folds, tears or errors in the original field mapping.

# Setup

Replace the example full paths in each section with your own. No Git repository, particular working directory or shared setup objects are required. Run the code chunks interactively after editing those paths; they are disabled during rendering.

Map generation and coordinate transformations use base R. Only the point clicker requires `magick`. Each section loads the script it needs where it is used.

# Optional helper: create a practice paper map once

Skip this section entirely if you already have a map. Nothing later depends on this code or its R objects.

The example is a 10 × 10 m map with four 5 × 5 m subquadrats, 40 random interior points and six extra points: two on the outer border, two on internal divisions and two slightly outside. Blank fields and unlabelled points allow handwritten details and identifiers before scanning.

Choose the full output path below; for the fgeo2 example, keep the PDF in `data_examples/coordinate_recovery_tutorial/`. Print it, add the handwritten information and scan it to a separate PDF. The following sections accept any scanned map PDF, whether simulated or real.

**The generator is disabled by default: change `#| eval: FALSE` to `#| eval: TRUE` to enable it for one render, then back to `FALSE` after creating the PDF.** You can also run the chunk manually. Rerunning it replaces the printable PDF, not the separately saved scan.

```{r}
#| label: generate-practice-map
#| eval: FALSE

map.pdf = "/full/path/to/maps/practice-map.pdf"
seed = 123
number.interior = 40
set.seed(seed)

practice.points <- data.frame(
	x = runif(number.interior, 0.3, 9.7),
	y = runif(number.interior, 0.3, 9.7)
)

# Two outer-border points, two internal-border points and two exterior points.
practice.points <- rbind(practice.points, data.frame(
	x = c(0, 10, 5, runif(1, 1, 9), -0.3, 10.3),
	y = c(runif(2, 1, 9), runif(1, 1, 9), 5, 3, 7)
))

dir.create(dirname(map.pdf), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
pdf(map.pdf, width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
par(mar = c(1, 1, 1, 1))
plot(
	NA, xlim = c(-1.5, 11.5), ylim = c(-3, 16), asp = 1,
	axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i"
)

text(-1, 15.3, "Practice field map: 10 x 10 m", adj = 0, font = 2)
text(-1, 14.2, "Plot: __________________    Quadrat: __________________", adj = 0)
text(-1, 13.2, "Mapped by: ______________    Checked by: ______________", adj = 0)
text(-1, 12.2, "Date: __________________    Census: __________________", adj = 0)

rect(0, 0, 10, 10, lwd = 1.5)
segments(5, 0, 5, 10, lty = 2, col = "grey60")
segments(0, 5, 10, 5, lty = 2, col = "grey60")
axis(1, at = c(0, 5, 10), labels = c("0", "5", "10 m"), pos = 0)
axis(2, at = c(0, 5, 10), labels = c("0", "5", "10 m"), pos = 0, las = 1)
points(practice.points$x, practice.points$y, pch = 20, cex = 0.7)
text(c(-0.8, -0.8, 10.7, 10.7), c(-1.1, 10.5, 10.5, -1.1), LETTERS[1:4])
arrows(10.7, 10.7, 10.7, 11.5, length = 0.08)
text(10.7, 11.8, "N")
text(-1, -1.8, "Notes: __________________________________________________", adj = 0)
text(-1, -2.6, "_________________________________________________________", adj = 0)
dev.off()
```

# Obtain clicked coordinates

Load the clicker here and run it interactively, not while rendering. Use your scanned map PDF as input. Name the four corners `corner_A`, `corner_B`, `corner_C` and `corner_D`, clockwise from the lower-left corner, and use the handwritten identifiers for the mapped points.

Click a point, type its label in the R console and press Enter. Press Esc or **Finish** when done. The clicker saves columns `label`, `x` and `y` after every point and refuses to overwrite an existing CSV.

```{r}
#| label: click-points
#| eval: FALSE
#| purl: false

source("/full/path/to/georeference.R")

map.pdf = "/full/path/to/maps/map-scanned.pdf"
clicked.csv = "/full/path/to/maps/map-clicked.csv"

clicked <- point_clicker(
	image.path = map.pdf,
	csv.path = clicked.csv
)
```

## Optional: continue using ImageJ

ImageJ or [Fiji](https://imagej.net/software/fiji/downloads) can collect the points instead; the historical workflow used a modified [PointPicker plugin](https://ctfs.si.edu/Public/DatabaseSetup/Resources/imageJ/pointpicker-modified3.zip). Save the exported coordinates as a CSV with columns `label`, `x` and `y`, using the same corner labels. Either transformation below can read that CSV. The direction of the image y-axis does not matter if every control is identified correctly.

# Recommended method: homography

Homography uses at least four controls and can correct photographic perspective. Here the four corners describe a 10 × 10 m quadrat whose lower-left corner is at global coordinates `(50, 50)` m. Enter the actual global coordinates for your own map.

This section reads the clicked CSV directly; it does not require the clicker to have been run in the same R session. The result and output CSV contain global coordinates directly, including points outside the mapped quadrat.

```{r}
#| label: apply-homography
#| eval: FALSE

source("/full/path/to/georeference.R")

clicked.csv = "/full/path/to/maps/map-clicked.csv"
output.csv = "/full/path/to/maps/map-homography-global.csv"

clicked <- read.csv(clicked.csv, colClasses = c(label = "character"))
names(clicked)[names(clicked) == "label"] <- "id"
stopifnot(!anyNA(clicked$id), all(nzchar(clicked$id)), !anyDuplicated(clicked$id))

known.controls <- data.frame(
	id = paste0("corner_", LETTERS[1:4]),
	x = c(50, 50, 60, 60),
	y = c(50, 60, 60, 50)
)

# Match controls by identifier, not by file row order.
control.order <- match(known.controls$id, clicked$id)
stopifnot(!anyNA(control.order))

known.xy.of.controls <- as.matrix(known.controls[, c("x", "y")])
clicked.xy.of.controls <- as.matrix(clicked[control.order, c("x", "y")])

is.control <- clicked$id %in% known.controls$id
clicked.xy.of.points <- as.matrix(clicked[!is.control, c("x", "y")])
rownames(clicked.xy.of.points) <- clicked$id[!is.control]

homography.xy <- apply_homography_transformation(
	known.xy.of.controls = known.xy.of.controls,
	clicked.xy.of.controls = clicked.xy.of.controls,
	clicked.xy.of.points = clicked.xy.of.points
)

recovered <- data.frame(
	id = rownames(homography.xy),
	global.x = homography.xy[, "x"],
	global.y = homography.xy[, "y"],
	row.names = NULL
)

write.csv(recovered, output.csv, row.names = FALSE)
head(recovered)
```

If controls are declared in local coordinates instead, convert the results with `compile_points_from_quadrats()` from the [quadrat code](https://github.com/gabrielareto/fgeo2/blob/main/03_spatial/R/new/quadrats.R), as explained in the [quadrat tutorial](https://github.com/gabrielareto/fgeo2/blob/main/03_spatial/tutorials/quadrats.qmd).

```{r}
#| label: fig-recovered-points
#| eval: FALSE
#| fig-cap: "Recovered global coordinates. The square marks the control locations."
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 5

plot(
	recovered$global.x,
	recovered$global.y,
	asp = 1,
	xlab = "Global plot x (m)",
	ylab = "Global plot y (m)",
	pch = 20
)
polygon(known.controls$x, known.controls$y, border = "red", lwd = 2)
```

## Optional quick error check

If independently known reference points are available, supply a CSV with `id`, `x` and `y` in global metres. These can be a subset of the mapped points, but must not be fitted controls. Otherwise skip this check; it does not depend on the practice-map generator.

```{r}
#| label: check-homography
#| eval: FALSE

known.points <- read.csv(
	"/full/path/to/maps/check-points-global.csv",
	colClasses = c(id = "character")
)
check.order <- match(known.points$id, recovered$id)
stopifnot(
	nrow(known.points) > 0, !anyDuplicated(known.points$id),
	!anyNA(check.order), !any(known.points$id %in% known.controls$id)
)

error.cm <- 100 * sqrt(
	(recovered$global.x[check.order] - known.points$x)^2 +
	(recovered$global.y[check.order] - known.points$y)^2
)

round(c(
	mean.error.cm = mean(error.cm),
	median.error.cm = median(error.cm),
	maximum.error.cm = max(error.cm)
), 1)
```

# Plan B: affine transformation

An affine transformation needs at least three non-collinear controls. Use it for a flat or nearly flat image when a corner is missing or unusually unreliable, not for appreciable photographic perspective. If more reliable controls are available, retain them.

This section is independent of the homography section: it loads the script and clicked CSV again, declares global controls and returns global coordinates directly. The example uses A, B and C; add `"corner_D"` to `available.controls` when it is usable.

```{r}
#| label: apply-affine
#| eval: FALSE

source("/full/path/to/georeference.R")

clicked.csv = "/full/path/to/maps/map-clicked.csv"
output.csv = "/full/path/to/maps/map-affine-global.csv"
available.controls = c("corner_A", "corner_B", "corner_C")

clicked <- read.csv(clicked.csv, colClasses = c(label = "character"))
names(clicked)[names(clicked) == "label"] <- "id"
stopifnot(!anyNA(clicked$id), all(nzchar(clicked$id)), !anyDuplicated(clicked$id))

known.controls <- data.frame(
	id = paste0("corner_", LETTERS[1:4]),
	x = c(50, 50, 60, 60),
	y = c(50, 60, 60, 50)
)

known.order <- match(available.controls, known.controls$id)
control.order <- match(available.controls, clicked$id)
stopifnot(!anyNA(known.order), !anyNA(control.order))

known.xy.of.controls <- as.matrix(known.controls[known.order, c("x", "y")])
clicked.xy.of.controls <- as.matrix(clicked[control.order, c("x", "y")])

# Exclude all corner records, including D when it is not used for fitting.
is.control <- clicked$id %in% known.controls$id
clicked.xy.of.points <- as.matrix(clicked[!is.control, c("x", "y")])
rownames(clicked.xy.of.points) <- clicked$id[!is.control]

affine.xy <- apply_affine_transformation(
	known.xy.of.controls = known.xy.of.controls,
	clicked.xy.of.controls = clicked.xy.of.controls,
	clicked.xy.of.points = clicked.xy.of.points
)

affine.recovered <- data.frame(
	id = rownames(affine.xy),
	global.x = affine.xy[, "x"],
	global.y = affine.xy[, "y"],
	row.names = NULL
)

write.csv(affine.recovered, output.csv, row.names = FALSE)
head(affine.recovered)
```

## Optional quick error check

Read the independent reference coordinates again; this check does not require the homography section or its error check.

```{r}
#| label: check-affine
#| eval: FALSE

known.points <- read.csv(
	"/full/path/to/maps/check-points-global.csv",
	colClasses = c(id = "character")
)
check.order <- match(known.points$id, affine.recovered$id)
stopifnot(
	nrow(known.points) > 0, !anyDuplicated(known.points$id),
	!anyNA(check.order), !any(known.points$id %in% known.controls$id)
)

affine.error.cm <- 100 * sqrt(
	(affine.recovered$global.x[check.order] - known.points$x)^2 +
	(affine.recovered$global.y[check.order] - known.points$y)^2
)

round(c(
	mean.error.cm = mean(affine.error.cm),
	median.error.cm = median(affine.error.cm),
	maximum.error.cm = max(affine.error.cm)
), 1)
```

# Optional: historical CTFS bug fix

The CTFS/ImageJ conversion is not the recommended pipeline and will not be retained in fgeo2. The archived [`imageJ.r` implementation](https://github.com/gabrielareto/fgeo2/blob/main/evaluation/Condit/topography/imageJ.r) remains available with its [geometry dependencies](https://github.com/gabrielareto/fgeo2/blob/main/evaluation/Condit/utilities/geometry.r). The original workflow is documented in the 2011 CTFS [PDF tutorial](https://ctfs.si.edu/ctfsdev/CTFSRPackageNew/files/tutorials/imageJTutorial/imageJ.pdf) and [HTML tutorial](https://ctfs.si.edu/ctfsdev/CTFSRPackageNew/index.php/web/tutorials/imageJTutorial/index.html).

The archived `distance.to.side()` passes one-column data frames instead of numeric intersection coordinates. If the old workflow is still required, run the following session-only replacement after loading the archived CTFS scripts. It fixes that one bug only. It does not fix inconsistent corner defaults, exterior points folded into a quadrat, or other limitations of the legacy workflow. Supply all four corner labels explicitly when calling the old functions.

```{r}
#| label: legacy-ctfs-fix
#| eval: false
#| purl: false

source("/full/path/to/Condit/utilities/geometry.r")
source("/full/path/to/Condit/topography/imageJ.r")

distance.to.side.original <- distance.to.side

distance.to.side <- function(pt, target, side1, side2)
{
	perpendicular <- perpendicular.distance(
		b = target[1], m = target[2], x = pt[1], y = pt[2]
	)

	parallel <- drop(as.matrix(parallel.line(
		b = side1[1], m = side1[2], x = pt[1], y = pt[2]
	)))
	intersection <- intersection.of.lines(
		b1 = parallel[1], m1 = parallel[2],
		b2 = target[1], m2 = target[2]
	)
	distance1 <- xydist(pt[1], pt[2], intersection$x, intersection$y)

	parallel <- drop(as.matrix(parallel.line(
		b = side2[1], m = side2[2], x = pt[1], y = pt[2]
	)))
	intersection <- intersection.of.lines(
		b1 = parallel[1], m1 = parallel[2],
		b2 = target[1], m2 = target[2]
	)
	distance2 <- xydist(pt[1], pt[2], intersection$x, intersection$y)

	distances <- c(perpendicular, distance1, distance2)
	c(mean(distances), sd(distances) / mean(distances))
}

stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
	unname(distance.to.side(
		pt = c(5, 5),
		target = c(0, Inf),
		side1 = c(10, 0),
		side2 = c(0, 0)
	)),
	c(5, 0)
)))
```
